header.name: Design Futures
header.description: This course will provide a theoretical and practical understanding of an emerging discipline in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) known as Design Furtures (aka Speculative Design and Critical Design Fiction). Students will read and critique case studies from the Design Futures corpus. There will be studio time for developing skills in creating future scenarios, making future prototypes, and creating design fiction videos that depict the implications and consequences, both postive and negative, of future design scenarios. This is a studio course held once per week in a 3 hour block that will combine both discussion and practical exercises.
prerequisites_desirable: Research Methods in Social Science and Design

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to discuss and distinguish design fiction methodologies.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to critique current human-technology configurations and their impacts on society and culture.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to create provocative and speculative future scenarios that highlight potential changes (positive and negative) that technologies may bring to social and cultural life in both the near-term and far-off futures.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to ideate, prototype, and evaluate new Design Future scenarios as part of individual and group assignments.

lecture_topics: Introduction to Design Futures: Speculative Design and Critical Design Fiction
Future Studies: Origin of Design Futures
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Write a one page 'what-if scenario' that explores possible probable, or preposterous near futures and how technologies might shape them.

lecture_topics: Methods: World Building in Design Futures
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Write a one page scenario that explores both a utopian and a distopian outcome of a future technology.
Write a one page 'mis-use /reuse scenario' that explores how an ordinary object that exists today might be used in unexpected way (in a manner it wasn't designed for).
Identify a community you would ilke to work with on a Participatory Design project with. Write a 2-4 page proposal for how you would engage that community in a Design Futures workshop.

lecture_topics: Case study: Human relationships with Artifical Intelligence Systems
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: In pairs: Design an AI interface that makes decisions on behalf of humans. Create a short video that follows a user of the application and the world.

lecture_topics: Case study: Human relationships with Smart Cities
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: In pairs: Design a Smart City interface that depicts how people engage in this new world (e.g. transportation, pollution, climate change, consumption, etc.).

lecture_topics: Design Futuring: Defining the world as it currently is today
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Write a brief research report (4-8 pages) describing the historical and current state of the domain your project will explore. Include the political, economic, ecological, material, behavioural, historical, and social dimensions.

lecture_topics: Design Futuring: Creating a proposed world with the technologies and interactions within it
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Develop a storyworld scenario that explains how the imagined technical object might transform human interaction, beliefs, attitudes, and the social system. Develop one utopian and one dystopian scenario.

lecture_topics: Design Futuring: Prototyping storyworlds, interfaces, and interaction
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Create a storyboard that depicts how characters in your future world engage with the proposed technology.

lecture_topics: Discussion: Readings, Case Studies & Practical: Open Studio
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Build an immersive prototype video, visual, or three-dimensional prototype that depicts potential interactions (positive or negative) with the technology.
